primer.text: Motion is the other place energy hides. One lesson prices it: the kinetic store of any moving object, set by its mass and by the square of its speed, with a worked calculation that keeps the squaring and the rounding honest.

modules.title: The kinetic store and the KE equation
modules.opening: Anything moving holds energy in its kinetic store. The store's size depends on two inputs — the object's mass and its speed — but the speed input is squared, which makes fast objects dramatically richer in energy than slow ones of the same mass.
keyPoints: Kinetic energy is the energy a moving object carries, set by its mass and its speed.
Every moving object carries energy in its kinetic store, whatever it is doing.
KE = ½ × m × v², with mass in kilograms and speed in metres per second.
The speed input is squared, so doubling the speed quadruples the energy in the kinetic store.

low.restatement: Mass and pace set the holding: double the cargo and the store doubles, but double the pace and it quadruples. The squaring is what makes road-speed choices matter so much.
low.analogy: A warehouse whose contents grow with the cargo mass but with the square of the conveyor's pace — hurry the belt and the stockpile explodes four-fold per doubling.
low.examPointer: Square the speed before multiplying, and quote the energy in joules; the classic error is using the bare speed once.

medium.restatement: The kinetic store is priced by KE = ½mv²: mass enters linearly in kilograms, speed enters squared in metres per second. Because of the square, equal speed doublings quadruple the stored energy, while equal mass doublings only double it.
medium.analogy: Insurance premiums that grow with the square of engine speed: modest pace increases buy disproportionately large energy bills.
medium.examPointer: In comparisons, change one input at a time and state the proportionality — 'speed doubled, so the store quadrupled' — to collect the reasoning mark.

glossary.definition: The energy an object has as a result of its mass and speed.
The energy store of a moving object; its size grows with mass and with the square of speed.
The rounded form used to quote a calculated answer to a stated precision.

workedExample.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy stored in a vehicle of mass 1200 kg moving at a speed of 27 m/s.
steps: List the known quantities: mass m = 1200 kg and speed v = 27 m/s.
Substitute into KE = ½ × m × v²: KE = 0.5 × 1200 × 729 = 437 400 J.
Round the final answer to 2 significant figures: KE = 440 000 J.
workedExample.finalAnswer: The kinetic store of the vehicle holds about 440 000 J.
